key_insight: Quenching medium dominates weld performance in SMAW of mild steel, far more than groove angle, and air cooling yields the best overall energy absorption and toughness.
engineering_relevance: For welded joints, post-weld cooling choice is a much stronger lever than groove angle when balancing strength, ductility, and toughness.
method: Analyzed AISI/SAE 1020 SMAW joints across 55–60° single-V groove angles and three quenching media: air, water, palm oil.
Used effect-share analysis, four multi-criteria decision methods, and machine-learning surrogates of stress–strain data.
Recovered derived metrics including modulus of toughness and Hollomon strain-hardening exponent from the reported tensile records.
evidence_signal: Across six mechanical responses, quenching medium explained 70.3–94.6% of the estimated effect, while groove angle contributed only 4.4–25.7% and interaction stayed below 3.2%; all four decision methods gave the same ranking.
watch_item: The reported rankings depend on reconstructed specimen geometry and derived stress–strain metrics, so implementation should verify the original tensile data and test conditions before generalizing.
paper_title: Groove angle and quenching medium in shielded metal arc welding of mild steel: Multi-criteria decision analysis, machine learning and energy absorption
